CheckTitle: Ensure all expired SSL/TLS certificates stored in AWS IAM are removed
Description: Expired SSL/TLS server certificates stored in IAM must be removed. Retaining expired certificates indicates gaps in certificate lifecycle management and poses risks of service disruption or, in misconfigured systems, potential use of expired trust anchors.
Risk: Expired certificates stored in IAM may be accidentally redeployed, causing TLS handshake failures or allowing authentication with an expired trust anchor. Failure to remove expired certificates signals immature PKI lifecycle management, which is a higher-order governance risk.
Remediation: Delete all expired server certificates from IAM using the AWS CLI: aws iam delete-server-certificate --server-certificate-name <name>. Implement automated alerting for certificate expiry 30 days in advance.
SeverityBasis: CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0.0 Control 1.19 (Level 1); NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 SC-17 (Public Key Infrastructure Certificates)
AuthoritativeSource: CIS Amazon Web Services Foundations Benchmark v3.0.0; NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5
